ModMetaData.name: Armory
ModMetaData.author: Kruecke
ModMetaData.description:
Armory is a weapon inspector and automatic manager for RimWorld 1.6. It shows what every colonist wants to carry, why they are not carrying it, and what the colony should craft, research or buy next.
Every free colonist gets range-aware rankings based on RimWorld's real accuracy curve, plus a ranged role (CQB, Assault, Line or Marksman) that can be overridden per colonist. Armory also assigns a hand type: Ranged or Melee. Simple Sidearms' primary mode wins when present; otherwise an explicit per-colonist choice wins, then a bonded weapon, a ranged-blocking shield belt, Brawler, shooting/melee passion, and finally skill. Only weapons of that hand type compete, so melee and ranged are never compared, and a colonist holding the wrong type is automatically switched to the best ready weapon of the chosen type unless a bonded weapon locks the hand. With Simple Sidearms, Armory also models one opposite-type backup. Blockers stay visible instead of hiding candidates: forbidden, outside the allowed area, unreachable, reserved, biocoded, role restrictions, ideoligion dislike, and Simple Sidearms slot or mass limits.
The Upgrades tab lists every obtainable weapon that would improve a colonist, grouped into Craft, Research and Buy. It shows owned and missing copies, expected gain and the best bench, and can queue one bill when a built bench can make the missing weapon. The Weapons tab covers every loose weapon on the map, while the Colonists tab shows each pawn's current hand and backup weapon, status and ranked alternatives. Double-click a colonist or loose weapon row to close Armory and jump to it on the map.
When no other weapon manager is active, automatic weapon management is on by default. Armory queues equip jobs for the best ready weapon, claims each weapon for one pawn, respects a swap cooldown, never unforbids anything, and treats unbonded persona weapons as manual-only. With Simple Sidearms, backup management keeps one legal opposite-type weapon and upgrades only the worst same-type weapon. Armory never adds a second backup; if extras are already carried, it reports them instead of adding more, and unusable biocoded backups are ignored when comparing upgrades. Automatic equipping and backup management can each be disabled in settings, and the Log tab records every decision with its reason.
Simple Sidearms support is optional and read through reflection, so Armory still works without it. No Harmony dependency.
